data.body:
`_end_open_operation_spans()` now `.end()`s (and thus exports) every operation-level span still open at invocation end, but `on_operation_start`/`on_operation_end`/`on_operation_replay` are unchanged and still always use the *deterministic* span ID `operation_id_to_span_id(execution_arn, operation_id)` (the default `deterministic=True` in `_start_span`) regardless of `info.is_replayed` or whether a span for that operation was already exported.

Concretely: operation A (WAIT/CALLBACK/CHAINED_INVOKE/STEP/CONTEXT) starts and suspends in invocation N — its deterministic-ID span is now ended+exported here. If A is still non-terminal in invocation N+1, `on_operation_replay` re-fires `on_operation_start` for it (same deterministic ID), and if it suspends again this method exports it *again* with the same ID. When A finally completes, `on_operation_end`'s `span is None` cross-invocation fallback also reuses the same deterministic ID. The result is multiple exported spans sharing one `span_id`+`trace_id` for any multi-invocation operation, which most tracing backends treat as invalid/ambiguous. This contradicts the plugin's own test `test_cross_invocation_operation_end_uses_deterministic_span_id` ('Exported exactly once...'), which never exercises the new suspend-then-reappear path this change enables.

`InvocationOtelPlugin` already solves this correctly (pre-existing, unaffected by this PR): it passes `existed=info.is_replayed` / `existed=True` so a replayed or cross-invocation-completed operation gets a fresh random span ID plus a `Link` back to the deterministic logical-operation context instead of reusing the ID. `ExecutionOtelPlugin` needs the equivalent — stop using the deterministic span ID once an operation has been replayed or is being stitched across invocations, and add a link to the deterministic operation context for correlation — before it's safe to end these spans at invocation boundaries.
